newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania president postpones election decree.
newsitem.headline: Albania president postpones election decree.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha on Wednesday postponed the signing of a decree to call new elections for the end of June, which most opposition parties had threatened to boycott, the president's office said.

Berisha earlier said he would dissolve parliament on Wednesday and sign the decree to call the elections, seen as vital to prevent Albania sliding back into violent unrest after riots in February and March.
"The decree will be signed as soon as the conditions for parliament to be dissolved are right," Berisha's spokeswoman told Reuters. "The decree will not be for now."

The early elections are a key part of the international effort to restore stability to Albania. The former communist country slid into anarchy after the collapse of high-yielding pyramid investment schemes earlier this year.

Most parties said they would refuse to take part in the elections on Berisha's terms as they were not happy with a new electoral law which was pushed through parliament by his former ruling Democratic Party on Tuesday.
They said they wanted an electoral law which was approved by all members of the national unity government, formed amid the riots in March as a way to calm the country.
